newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom drags NZ share market lower at close.
newsitem.headline: Telecom drags NZ share market lower at close.

text.p: * Telecom drags NZ share prices lower at close
* Market studiously ignores Wall Street rally
A sharp fall-off in Telecom brought a quick turnaround for the New Zealand share market on Friday, the top 40 index ending lower after a strong start.
By the close the NZSE-40 Capital Index was off 15.97 at 2,323.18 on turnover worth NZ$62 million.
The index had earlier hit a peak of 2,345.01 as concerns about Telecom's third quarter earnings dissipated.
But a downgrade by Standard and Poor's later in the day put paid to any further strength, Telecom ending 11 cents down at NZ$6.91 and a far cry from its session high of NZ$7.06.
Earnings concerns mid-way through the reporting season continued to dog the market overall and effectively nullify any possible benefit from yet another record run on Wall Street.

Telecom aside, the remaining leaders were mostly steady, with Brierley Investments holding well at NZ$1.36 despite some last minute selling. Lion Nathan staged a partial rebound by gaining two cents to NZ$3.62.
Carter Holt Harvey also fared reasonably, easing just one to NZ$3.29.
Jim Patterson at First NZ Capital said Telecom's downgrade to AA from AA plus was the turning point on the day.
"We really saw the stock come off in a hurry from there," he said.
There was also a lot of Telecom stock around, with 1.26 million shares crossing at NZ$6.93 each.
Telecom also topped the turnvoer list with 4.0 million shares, worth NZ$27.9 million, trading.
Patterson said a turnaround in the fortunes of the Australian market, where by 4.10 a.m. (0310 GMT) the All Ords was down 11.5 at 2,484.9, also played a part.
